Hi Joel / Ananya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from today
- Goal: POC Redwood Private in your VPC with air-gap feasibility for PHI workloads.
- Primary concerns: control plane isolation, KMS/HSM integration, ingress/egress network controls, and audit logs for compliance teams.

Redwood differentiators we covered
- Private control plane option: runs in-customer VPC with minimal outbound needs (or fully air-gapped on-prem installer for locked environments).
- Flexible KMS/HSM integrations (bring-your-own KMS, HSM-backed keywrap).
- Transparent audit logs and token-level tracing in the Console for compliance and e-discovery.
- Network-first design: explicit CIDRs/ports for allowlisting + guidance for prefix/KV cache placement to preserve latency without exposing control channels.

Suggested next technical tests
1) IP allowlist smoke test — confirm outbound endpoints and ports from your test subnet (we provide CIDRs).
2) Control plane connectivity toggle — run an isolated deployment with private control plane (no public control plane traffic).
3) Air-gap feasibility runbook walkthrough — review installer artifacts and telemetry options (on-prem package).
4) KMS proof-of-concept — validate keywrap and rotation with your KMS.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_one-pager.pdf, networking-checklist.xlsx, airgap-install-test-plan.md (short stubs attached).

Can we book a technical deep-dive next week with your infra and security leads? Marissa (Solutions Eng) and Aditya (Infra Eng) will join to run through the test plan. I can do Wed 8/2 or Thu 8/3 afternoon PT — let me know what works.

Also: Joel, per your ask, I included a concise comparison vs hyperscalers in the one-pager — quick callout: hyperscalers often provide managed endpoints with simple onboarding but limited options for fully air-gapped control planes and constrained KMS/HSM integrations.

Thanks — talk soon.

Joel — great questions. Answers and concrete next steps below.

1) Control plane / air-gap options
- Fully air-gapped: yes — our on-prem airgap installer delivers a self-contained control plane and runtime with zero outbound telemetry by default. That is the model customers use when they require FIPS-level isolation.
- Private control plane in VPC: this is our more common configuration for regulated customers. The control plane runs in your VPC, we provide an optional small set of egress endpoints (registry/updates) which can be restricted to specific CIDRs. Telemetry is configurable and can be disabled or routed to your collector.

2) KMS/HSM
- Supported integrations: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault + HSM-backed keywrap, HashiCorp Vault (HSM-backed) + PKCS#11 wrappers.
- Key material: we never escrow customer master keys on Redwood-managed infrastructure for Private deployments. For VPC/private control plane setups keys are stored/managed by your KMS; in air-gapped on-prem installs the key material stays in your HSM (we support keywrap so secrets are never exposed to Redwood).

3) Networking specifics (IP allowlist smoke test)
- We'll provide a short allowlist file with the minimal egress CIDRs and ports (TCP 443 plus management ports as needed). Expected primary CIDR: 52.34.120.0/22 (example) — full list in the attached networking-checklist.xlsx.
- Cross-AZ/cache placement: to avoid latency you can colocate KV cache and inference nodes in the same subnet/AZ. If cache is in another AZ, expect a 5–15ms delta depending on AZ pairing; we’ll work with your infra to optimize placement.

4) Short procurement-friendly differentiators vs hyperscalers (one-pager)
- Air-gap capability: hyperscalers typically cannot provide a fully air-gapped, self-contained control plane.
- KMS/HSM flexibility: broader vendor support and no escrow of customer master keys for our Private deployments.
- Observable unit economics: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and fine-grained rollout controls for predictable production behavior.

Next steps I propose
- [A] IP allowlist smoke test: we’ll send the CIDR list today; you run the test and share reachability by EOD Mon.
- [B] Technical deep-dive: Marissa (solutions) + Aditya (infra) + your infra/security. Proposed slots: Wed 2026-09-02 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2026-09-03 1:00–2:00 PT — which works?
- [C] KMS POC: once network is green, we’ll do a 1–2 hour KMS proof with your Vault/KMS team.

Attachments: updated networking-checklist.xlsx (with CIDRs), airgap-install-test-plan.md (step-by-step).

If helpful I can also prepare a short one-pager specifically for procurement summarizing the differences between Redwood Private and the hyperscaler managed endpoints — I’ve attached the generic one-pager but can tailor it.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Aditya in to confirm availability.

Best,
Vanessa
